brief: PJM and ERCOT both set all-time peak demand records this summer, but only PJM saw prices react. PJM's July heat wave pushed load to 168/162 GW gross/net of demand response, beating its 2006 record and its 154 GW forecast, with real-time prices spiking above $2,000/MWh; a smaller mid-July peak of 159 GW also topped $1,000/MWh. Forwards stayed strong even as conditions calmed afterward. ERCOT's 91 GW record, above both last year's peak and this year's forecast, saw only low-hundreds pricing because renewables and storage covered the load, and forwards have since weakened, especially after Governor Abbott's letter paused the Batch Zero review, pushing the ERCOT curve into contango. Elsewhere, MISO grew in line with forecast while New York and California undershot. Global gas turbine orders hit a record 38 GW in Q2, up 71% YoY, led by North American demand. Wolfe holds its sentiment meter flat at "2", flagging PJM's proposed RBP cost allocation on existing-PPA load as a risk still pending FERC, while noting CEG's tone keeps improving and Vistra's Cogentrix deal cleared FERC.
